content:
Donald Trump drew backlash on Thursday over a comment about when his war with Iran will end, which he made during a Thanksgiving call with U.S. service members.

Speaking from his Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida to a service member stationed in the Middle East, Trump said he and first lady Melania Trump “join millions this holiday to pray for your safety and success.”

“You’re going to continue that deployment and we have victory at hand,” he continued.

As for when that victory might come in the conflict he launched nine months ago, Trump said: “It’s going to be — whenever, sort of, whenever I want it to be.”

“To be honest, we’re trying to be nice, we’re trying to let them, we’re giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives,” he added of ongoing negotiations with Iran.

“But I’m not sure if they are going to take advantage of that. Some people question why, are they crazy? Maybe they are,” he said.

Critics seized on Trump’s suggestion that the timing of the war’s conclusion was effectively his to decide, with one describing his remarks as “despicable.”

Trump, after launching the war in February, initially said it would last a matter of weeks. It continues.

“Just the message service members want to hear on Thanksgiving while away from their families fighting his war of choice,” one wrote on X.
